newsitem.title: UK: British Chambers say rate rise blow to exporters.
newsitem.headline: British Chambers say rate rise blow to exporters.

text.p: The British Chambers of Commerce (BCC) said a quarter-point rise in interest rates to 6.50 percent was yet another blow to exporters and urged Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown to raise taxes to take the pressure off monetary policy.
"This is no real surprise given the limitations placed on the Monetary Policy Committee," BCC deputy director-general Ian Peters said in a statement.

"But it will come as a further blow to Britain's export prospects if it results in further strengthening of sterling. It is now up to the Chancellor to remove pressure for further interest rate hikes by announcing modest increases to personal taxation in his July budget."
Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown will present his first budget on July 2.
